_comment: The benchmark corpus. Each entry must be PINNED to a commit SHA before it can be scored:
an unpinned run is not reproducible, and a benchmark you cannot reproduce cannot show a
regression. `npm run bench` refuses to score any repo whose `sha` is null.
Pin with:  node bench/pin.mjs            (resolves every null sha via the forge API)
and commit the result. Never move a pinned SHA without re-auditing that repo — the truth
file is keyed by SHA precisely so a moved pin cannot silently invalidate it.

notes: The regression case, and the reason this document exists.
Known ground truth: 3 real loop N+1s (core/views.py:878/880, core/views.py:156,
admin_views.py:1030/1048/1081), 1 real batch opportunity (testcases/views.py:285/422/426),
5 cold-path migrations that must NOT be reported as performance findings, and 2 JavaScript
files that must NOT be reported at all. Also the engine-inference case: MySQL only, no
Mongo, Redis, Hive, BigQuery, Redshift or OpenSearch.
Scale (~10k files), scope composition across files, and includes/preload already present
in places — so it tests that the tool does not 'fix' what is already batched. Exercises
the indentation-based scope reader on Ruby `.each do`.
Prisma fragments passed between modules — the case relevance.ts was written for. Tests
brace-based scope analysis, and tests that Array.prototype.find and Object.keys produce
zero candidates.

repos.stack: Java · Spring Data JPA · Hibernate · MySQL/H2
notes: Small enough (~50 source files) to hand-audit exhaustively, which makes it the only repo
where recall is measured against a complete truth set rather than a sampled one. Tests
@Query, derived query methods, and FetchType.LAZY N+1.
Multi-engine by design — the hardest case for Fix 3. EngineProfile.declared should return
all three and `primary` should be honest about the ambiguity rather than picking one. Also
the largest share of genuine raw SQL, so it is the control that proves Fix 4 did not break
the SQL path.

repos.stack: TypeScript · no data layer at all
notes: Not scored for recall. speeDB must report ZERO findings here, in words, and say so.
Before Fix 3 it would have found Object.keys().
